components.css: .ds-ledger-nav { display: flex; gap: 28px; color: var(--ink); font: 400 0.72rem/1 var(--mono); text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; } .ds-ledger-nav a { color: inherit; text-decoration: none; } .ds-ledger-nav a::after { display: block; width: 100%; height: 1px; margin-top: 6px; background: currentColor; content: ""; transform: scaleX(0); transform-origin: left; transition: transform 180ms ease-out; } .ds-ledger-nav a:hover { color: var(--green); } .ds-ledger-nav a:hover::after, .ds-ledger-nav a:focus-visible::after { transform: scaleX(1); } .ds-ledger-nav a:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--copper); outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Evidence Rail Fact
components.description: A ruled fact cell composed as part of a continuous evidence rail.
components.css: .ds-evidence-fact { min-height: 180px; padding: 30px 32px; border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 0; color: var(--ink); background: var(--paper); } .ds-evidence-fact span { display: block; color: var(--muted); font: 400 0.72rem/1 var(--mono); text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; } .ds-evidence-fact strong { display: block; margin-top: 30px; font: 520 clamp(2rem, 3.4vw, 3.25rem)/1 var(--display); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; letter-spacing: -0.025em; } .ds-evidence-fact small { display: block; margin-top: 11px; color: var(--muted); font: 400 0.78rem/1.4 var(--sans); }

components.name: Logarithmic Budget Ruler
components.description: Signature semantic SVG comparing selected p99 with the engineering budget on a true log scale.
components.css: .ds-budget-ruler { width: 300px; margin: 0; padding: 24px; border: 1px solid var(--ink); border-radius: 0; color: var(--muted); background: var(--paper-deep); font: 400 0.72rem/1.4 var(--mono); text-align: center; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; } .ds-budget-ruler svg { width: 100%; height: auto; overflow: visible; } .ds-ruler-spine { stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 1; } .ds-ruler-budget { stroke: var(--copper); stroke-width: 1.5; stroke-dasharray: 7 6; } .ds-ruler-budget-dot { fill: var(--copper); } .ds-ruler-budget-text { fill: var(--copper); font: 11px var(--mono); } .ds-ruler-measure { stroke: var(--green); stroke-width: 2; } .ds-ruler-measure-dot { fill: var(--green); stroke: var(--paper); stroke-width: 3; } .ds-ruler-measure-text { fill: var(--green); font: 600 11px var(--mono); }

narrative.overview:
The system turns benchmark claims into a sequence of inspectable evidence. It borrows the authority of an engineering ledger—warm uncoated paper, carbon ink, ruled partitions, binder marks, and disciplined data labels—while letting a few measured values reach editorial scale. The result should feel skeptical, precise, and materially grounded rather than like a generic analytics dashboard.

Persuasion comes from visible measurement boundaries, not decoration. A dominant result earns attention; provenance, methodology, units, comparison qualifiers, and semantic table equivalents earn trust. Verification green, comparison blue, and loss/budget copper remain functional annotations within an otherwise neutral field.
keyCharacteristics: Editorial-scale measurements paired with compact monospaced evidence labels.
Continuous ruled sections and unequal evidence fields instead of floating metric cards.
Square controls, hairline borders, and flat paper layers with no decorative elevation.
Semantic color reserved for verification, comparison, and budget or loss states.
Explicit synthetic-workload, paper-trading, provenance, and cross-host boundaries.

rules.name: The Evidence-Only Color Rule
rules.body: Verification green, comparison blue, and loss/budget copper communicate data or state; they do not decorate neutral regions.

rules.name: The Paper Field Rule
rules.body: Warm ledger paper remains the dominant ground. Pressed paper and verification wash create only the tonal distinctions already present in the ledger.

rules.name: The Measurement Leads Rule
rules.body: Large Newsreader numerals state the result; nearby Plex Mono labels, units, and qualifiers define exactly what was measured.

rules.name: The Mono Means Evidence Rule
rules.body: Use the monospaced face for operational labels, controls, provenance, navigation, and chart annotation—not for explanatory paragraphs.

rules.name: The Continuous Record Rule
rules.body: Major facts share borders and alignment in one evidence rail or ledger; do not split them into detached, equally weighted cards.

rules.name: The First-Viewport Proof Rule
rules.body: Preserve the pairing of the dominant p99 measurement, published-run control, scope stamp, and logarithmic budget ruler at every breakpoint, even when the ruler stacks below the measurement.

rules.name: The Flat Ledger Rule
rules.body: Surfaces remain in the paper plane; hierarchy is created by scale, rules, alignment, and tonal fields, never shadow.

rules.name: The Square Instrument Rule
rules.body: Buttons, selects, tooltip frames, bars, and content regions keep zero-radius corners.

dos: Do lead claims with dated measurements, visible units, and nearby provenance or methodology.
Do preserve the large-measurement and logarithmic-ruler pairing as the dashboard's focal proof.
Do use verification green, comparison blue, and loss/budget copper only for their implemented semantic roles.
Do provide semantic HTML or table equivalents for graphical evidence.
Do retain square corners, hairline partitions, and the continuous ledger reading order across breakpoints.
Do keep synthetic workload, paper trading, and no-live-orders scope visible.
donts: Don't convert the evidence rail into floating metric cards or add decorative shadows.
Don't present cross-host comparisons as same-machine performance trends.
Don't use semantic evidence colors as broad decorative accents.
Don't hide paper-trading, synthetic-data, measurement-boundary, or provenance qualifiers behind interaction.
Don't replace the logarithmic budget ruler with a visually convenient linear scale.
Don't round controls, bars, tooltips, or ledger containers.
